content:
Apple TV+ currently has a strong lineup of series, with flagship titles including "Slow Horses," "Ted Lasso," "Dark Matter," and the new comedy "Brothers" starring Matthew McConaughey. However, there are plenty more great shows to come. Below is an introduction to every new release premiering on Apple TV+ in October.

"The Last First: Winter K2"

  • Date: October 2
  • Type: Film
  • Category: Documentary

Directed by Amir Bar-Lev, "The Last First: Winter K2" tells a complex, thrilling, and moving story that examines the extreme mountaineering industry and its ever-evolving culture. The film focuses on a 2021 expedition featuring climbers including Icelandic mountaineer John Snorri Sigurjónsson, as well as the Pakistani father-and-son team Ali and Sajid Sadpara, whose goal was to become the first team to summit during winter—when K2 presents its harshest conditions. However, they soon discovered that on this perilous climbing route, they were also accompanied by influencer climbers and their filming crews, commercial expedition clients, and renowned Nepalese mountaineer Nims and his team of Sherpas. "The Last First: Winter K2" takes viewers straight to K2's frozen peaks and unpredictable weather, revealing an unexpected, layered story—one that weaves together strategy and determination, class and hierarchy, money and power—all unfolding in a life-or-death environment.

"The Sisters Grimm" (Season 2)

  • Date: October 2
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Kids and Family

Two orphaned sisters live in a town filled with fairy tale and fantasy characters, where they must face all kinds of heroes and villains while also investigating the mystery of their missing parents. "The Sisters Grimm" blends exploration, fantasy, and adventure elements to deliver important life lessons for viewers of all ages.

"Small Prophets"

  • Date: October 7
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Comedy

"Small Prophets" tells the comedic story of the eccentric Michael Sleep (played by Pearce Quigley). Ever since his beloved Clea disappeared seven years ago, he has been living a mundane life: working at a hardware store, visiting his father Brian (Sir Michael Palin), and hoping for Clea's return. One day, Brian shares with him an ancient recipe that requires rainwater, horse manure, and a touch of alchemical ingredients. Armed with the recipe, Michael sets out to (albeit half-heartedly) create "homunculi"—magical sprites that can predict the future—hoping they can answer the question on his mind: "Will I ever see Clea again?"

"Matchbox The Movie"

  • Date: October 9
  • Type: Film
  • Category: Action

Adapted from the classic Mattel toy, "Matchbox The Movie" is a thrilling global adventure action film that follows a group of friends who have known each other since childhood. Just as life is going on as usual, CIA undercover agent Sean (played by John Cena)—their long-lost former "leader"—suddenly returns to their small town, only to inadvertently drag them into a madcap international chase to save the world.

"Tenzing"

  • Date: October 16
  • Type: Film
  • Category: Drama

Based on a true story, "Tenzing" recounts a little-known tale of gifted Himalayan climber Tenzing Norgay (played by Genden Phuntsok), who, alongside New Zealand mountaineer Edmund Hillary (played by Tom Hiddleston), became one of the first people to successfully summit Mount Everest. Encouraged by his wife Dawa (played by Thinley Lhamo), Tenzing receives support from expedition secretary Jill Henderson (played by Caitríona Balfe). Together, they convince Colonel John Hunt (played by Willem Dafoe) to place Tenzing in a core position on the British climbing team rather than merely serving as a porter. Western climbers view "Everest" as a target to be conquered, while Tenzing reveres "Chomolungma" (Mount Everest) as a sacred goddess of the snow mountains. The subsequent ascent must navigate tensions between backgrounds, class, and ambition, as well as the dangers posed by the mountain itself. But at the top of the world, empires, status, and ambitions are all cast aside, leaving only two "outsiders" standing side by side out of mutual respect and trust—for Tenzing, this is both the fulfillment of a lifelong dream and the completion of a spiritual calling.

"Where's Wanda?" (Season 2)

  • Date: October 21
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Dark Comedy

Apple's first German-language series, "Where's Wanda?" is a dark comedy about Dedo and Carlotta Klatt's desperate search for their missing 17-year-old daughter Wanda, who vanished without a trace months earlier. After the police fail to solve the case, the family decides to take matters into their own hands, obtaining surveillance equipment with the help of their tech-savvy son Ole. They disguise themselves as utility company workers and install listening devices across the entire community and half the suburbs, only to discover that behind every front door, their neighbors are not at all what they seem.

"Nocturne"

  • Date: October 30
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Crime Drama

The series tells the story of Jonah Lynn (played by Liev Schreiber), a former veteran who turned homicide detective. Weary of chasing cases on the streets of Philadelphia, he moves to a small town in western Pennsylvania hoping for a quieter life. However, when the town and his family fall one by one to the machinations of cunning serial killer Jurek Walter (played by Graham), Jonah must do everything in his power to protect what he holds dear. When the desperate search for Jurek's last missing victim forces Jonah to send his proxy daughter, FBI agent Saga Bauer (played by Beetz), to take on Jurek, just how far will Jonah go?

New episodes of series including "Slow Horses" and "Brothers" to be released

Apple TV+ will also release new episodes of several currently airing series in October, including:

  • "Ted Lasso": The comedy starring Jason Sudeikis, with new episodes available through October 7
  • "Last Seen": A crime thriller, with new episodes available through October 7
  • "Slow Horses": The acclaimed British spy drama, with new episodes available through October 21
  • "Dark Matter": The sci-fi series starring Joel Edgerton, with new episodes available through October 30
  • "Brothers": The comedy featuring Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson, with new episodes available through November 4

Which Apple TV+ October release are you planning to watch? Let us know in the comments.

Apple TV+ costs US$14.99 per month (approximately HK$117), or can be obtained at a discounted rate through the Apple One bundle.
